text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The American inventor of the sewing machine, ELIAS HOWE, was born in 1819.
Australian physician, Dr MARY BOOTH, who founded the ANZAC Fellowship of Women and the Ex-servicewomen's club, was born in 1869.
Australia's first woman cabinet minister, Dame ENID LYONS, was born in 1897. She was also an author, and her work included "Among the Carrion Crows" and "The Old Haggis".
British romantic novelist, BARBARA CARTLAND, who has written more than 500 books, was born in 1901.
Former British prime minister and conservative politician, EDWARD HEATH, was born in 1916. He was prime minister from 1970 to 1974.

Australian singer and songwriter, BON SCOTT, was born in 1946. He started his career in the group the 'Valentines' and in the seventies he formed 'Fraternity". He is probably best known as leadsinger of 'AC/DC'. He replaced original lead singer DAVE EVANS in 1974 and stayed with the band until his death in 1980. He was replaced by BRIAN JOHNSON. 'AC/DC's biggest hit while SCOTT was leadsinger was "Touch Too Much" in 1980.

American singer, DEBBIE SLEDGE, was born in 1954. She was the eldest of the siblings in the group 'Sister Sledge'. Hits included "He's The Greatest Dancer" (1979), "We Are Family" (1979) and "Frankie" (1985).
** EVENTS **
1386 : In the Swiss-Swabian wars, LEOPOLD III and his
6,000-strong Austrian army was defeated by a force of only 1,600 Swiss pikemen at the battle of Sempach in a display of superior tactics.
1755 : In the Seven Years War, a force of British and
Virginians under General BRADDOCK were heavily defeated by a combined French and Indian attack at the Monogahela River near Fort Duquesne. BRADDOCK himself died in the battle.
1816 : Argentina proclaimed its independence from Spain
at the Congress of Tucuman.
1877 : The first lawn tennis championship was held at

Wimbledon. The men's singles game was played on the "top quality croquet lawns of the All-England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club". Rackets player SPENCER W. GORE won the title. Lawn tennis had only been invented in its current form for a few years. It was derived from the 12th century French game of real (or royal) tennis.
1915 : In World War One, South African forces under LOUIS
BOTHA forced the surrender of German forces in South West Africa.
1922 : Eighteen-year-old American swimmer, JOHNNY
WEISSMULLER, became the first man to swim 100 metres in less than a minute. His record breaking time was 58.6 seconds. WEISMULLER later starred as Tarzan in the series of movies.
1925 : In Dublin, 22-year-old OONAGH KEOGH became the
first female member of a stock exchange.
1932 : KING CAMP GILLETTE, U.S. inventor and manufacturer
of the safety razor, died.
1938 : 35 million gas masks were installed in British
shops in anticipation of the outbreak of war. (World War II)
1947 : The long-expected engagement of Princess ELIZABETH
to Lieutenant PHILIP MOUNTBATTEN R.N. was announced. Thousands of people cheered the couple as they appeared on the Buckingham Palace balcony. Princess ELIZABETH was 21 and Lieutenant
MOUNTBATTEN was 26. The government announced extra ration coupons for the Princess' wedding gown. The royal couple was married four months later at Westminister Abbey.
1951 : American crime writer, DASHIELL HAMMETT, was

jailed for contempt of court after refusing to give evidence before the Un-American Activities Committee. The committee was set up by Senator JOE McCARTHY in his crusade against Communism. HAMMETT's crime classics included "The Maltese Falcon" and "The Thin Man".
1953 : In Sydney's Central court a 63-year-old woman

appeared, charged with murdering four people. CAROLINE GRILLS was found guilty of poisoning her sister-in-law and three other people with thallium. Mrs GRILLS , who was dubbed "Aunt Thally", reportedly laughed frequently during the trial and appeared to enjoy the proceedings. The Crown Prosecutor told the court Mrs GRILLS was a practised poisoner who experienced a psychological thrill by watching her victims suffer. She was sentenced to death but her sentence was commuted.
1960 : In a speech, Soviet leader NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV
warned the United States against intervention in Cuba and said Soviet forces would support the Cuban people.
1962 : The trans-Tasman telephone cable between Sydney
and Auckland was opened.
1968 : One of Australia's longest sieges came to end
after Glenfield gunman, WALLY MELLISH, surrendered. The eight-day seige in Sydney included the gunman's wedding, with the Police Commissioner NORM ALLAN as his best man. A special

marriage licence was obtained and chaplain performed the ceremony to marry MELLISH and his girlfriend, BERYL MUDDLE. BERYL and her 11-month-old son were held hostage for the eight days. After his surrender, the new Mrs MELLISH was overheard telling police that she wanted a divorce.
1973 : In Uganda, IDI AMIN ordered the arrest and
expulsion of 112 Peace Corps workers.
1979 : The Civil war in Nicaragua ended with the
Sandinista rebels overthrowing General SOMOZA. His family had ruled Nicaragua for 47 years.
1984 : York Minster Cathedral was damaged after being

struck by lightning. Fire in the roof destroyed the south transept of the 700-year-old building. Quick work by clergy saved most of the treasures held in the Cathedral and stopped the blaze from spreading. Church critics claimed the lightning strike was an act of God, in retaliation over the consecration of unorthodox priest Right Reverend DAVID JENKINS as Bishop of
Durham.
1990 : Leaders of the world's seven largest industrial
nations began an economic summit in Houston with a call by U.S. President GEORGE BUSH to create "a new world of freedom".
1993 : British scientists using DNA genetic
fingerprinting tests, identified the bones of the Russian Tsar NICHOLAS II and members of his family.
1996 : Thousands of flag-waving children gave NELSON
MANDELA a hero's welcome to Britain, cheering and chanting his name as the South African president's state visit was launched in a blaze of royal pomp and ceremony.
1996 : Israeli Prime Minister BENJAMIN NETANYAHU used his
first visit to Washington to outline his views linking peace in the Middle East to Israel's security needs.
